components.name: Quality of professional work in the internship

rules: Penalties for incomplete, late, or incorrectly formatted assignments are at the professor's discretion.
Failure to receive the site supervisor's evaluation form results in NO CREDIT for the course, regardless of other work.
Minimum 50 work hours per credit hour; 3 credits = 150 hours minimum.
Blackboard point totals (5+5+5+5+10+100 = 130) are bookkeeping for the two weighted buckets, not the grade basis.
grading.source: IST 471 Syllabus.pdf p.5, pulled and extracted 2026-09-03 (bb_files 26, sha cf69c388..., 8 pages / 14723 chars in bb_file_text)
grading.verified: Seed 70/30 split, letter scale and late-penalty wording all match the pulled PDF exactly. No change made to weights or method.
grading.ai_policy: iSchool appendix 'Limited and Specified Artificial Intelligence Use' with the permitted-assignment placeholder left unfilled; appendix default therefore governs - no AI tool permitted on any assignment absent documented instructor permission. Written to grading_schemes.ai_policy.
grading.instrument: The 70% work-quality half is scored from Site Supervisor Evaluation.pdf (bb_files 61): 8 competencies rated 1-5, 8 IM&T learning outcomes rated S/D-SA-N/O, 4 narrative questions.

tree_shape.description: Three top-level nodes, no weeks and no modules. Content = course documents; Assignments = one Ultra test-link per numbered assignment, each carrying its own attachments in the instructions body; Introductions! = a course link to the single discussion forum. Nothing is dated or sequenced by week; the course is paced by the student's own internship hours.

media_links: Introductions! (course link -> discussion forum, no bytes)

tree_shape.new_file_rule: A new file next week will arrive as a data-bbfile attachment inside an Assignment N test-link's instructions body -> assignment_spec, linked to the matching IST.471/aN assignment. A new file dropped into Content is syllabus_policy only if its title says syllabus/policy; a form (Learning Agreement, evaluation) placed in Content is assignment_spec linked to the assignment that requires it.

notes: Pull complete. Whole corpus = 4 PDFs, all stored, mirrored and extracted (15 text units); needs_move=0. The decisive finding stands from v1: 3 of the 4 files were data-bbfile attachments inside assessment instruction bodies, which the summary crawl does not walk - the summary catalog had 1 of 4 files, so 75% of this course's corpus was invisible before the embed refresh. Zero stale URLs. Grading needed no change: the pulled syllabus confirmed the seed's 70/30 split, letter scale and late policy verbatim; the only grading write was the previously-null ai_policy. The three pulled forms are the real value of this pull - together they enumerate exactly which facts Stack must supply (site supervisor identity, work-block dates and schedule, faculty sponsor email, grading basis, academic advisor) before Assignments 1 and 4 can be completed, and they surfaced a 45-vs-50 hours-per-credit conflict between the Registrar form and the syllabus.

pull_result.note: The Learning Agreement did not land on the first batch fire and was re-fired once; it then landed. Downloads in this environment land as UUID .tmp files rather than Blackboard display names, so files were claimed by first-page text signature (pdftotext) rather than by filename.
